tickets.title: Evaluate closing Third Avenue L station
tickets.summary: A public speaker said the Third Avenue L stop has few riders getting on or off during rush hour, and his simulation of MTA trip data estimated that closing it would save New Yorkers about 1,800 hours a day. He asked the board to refer the idea to the transportation committee and to consider a pilot closure with the MTA. Action: Refer the Third Avenue stop closure proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about a pilot.

tickets.title: Enforcement and bike storage at 11th Street
tickets.requester: Chris Messb (public speaker); Keith Powers (State Assembly Member); District Manager (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Over 100 e-bikes used by food delivery workers are stored on 11th Street, blocking the street and sidewalk and possibly posing a fire hazard, according to a speaker who said businesses have closed. The precinct plans enforcement on October 7 that would confiscate bikes, while speakers asked for advance notice and multilingual outreach to workers and for a sanctioned storage site. Action: Work with the precinct and sanitation before October 7 on advance notice in multiple languages, a legal storage site, and sanitation pickups, and report back to the board.

tickets.title: Drug activity and dark spots in Seward Park
tickets.requester: Susan (District Manager); Parks committee report speaker (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Speakers reported increased drug use and homelessness in Seward Park, and the Lower East Side Ecology Center said it is in a building next to a bathroom frequented by drug users. Dark areas in the park were also raised as a place where drug use goes unseen. Action: Ask the Seventh Precinct and Parks to address drug activity and lighting, and assess whether mobile crisis teams could respond instead of police.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections
tickets.summary: A resolution would urge NYC public schools to pilot a mobile-first voting option for Community Education Council elections, since turnout is about 2% and many households rely only on smartphones. Speakers asked that outreach be multilingual and clearly state that immigration status is not collected, and that the voting option not replace in-person voting. Action: Vote on the resolution and send it to the Department of Education with a request for multilingual outreach and clear privacy language.

tickets.title: SLA application at 11 Allen Street
tickets.summary: The board voted 20 to 10 with 9 abstentions to recommend denial of a full liquor license for the Allen Street location, but the SLA could still approve it without stipulations if no one attends its hearing. Speakers cited nearby crowds and problems at the operator's former location. Action: The community board office will organize community members to attend the SLA hearing and seek elected official support for the denial.

tickets.title: Correct August SLA resolution wording
tickets.summary: Two August SLA resolutions wrongly state a full on-premises license where the applications were for beer and wine licenses, a clerical error noted by a board member. Item 10 is Softours Tea House and item 3 is Cozy Cafe. Action: Correct the August resolution wording for both items and send the corrected resolutions to the SLA.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP timing and terms
tickets.summary: The joint land use and economic development committee said EDC could not explain how the board's resolutions were included in the Essex Market RFP, which was due to go out at the end of the month. The committee asked EDC to postpone issuing it so the terms would reflect community market requirements. Action: Meet with EDC later this week to confirm the RFP terms and postpone its issuance, then update the board.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot locations
tickets.location_raw: Delansancy Plaza; Cooper Square at East Sixth Street and Third Avenue
tickets.summary: The city is installing two of 17 pilot free public restrooms in the district, at Delancey Plaza and Cooper Square, and DOT is the lead agency. The board raised concerns about who can access the restrooms and how emergency calls from inside would be handled. Action: Bring a resolution next month setting out the board's concerns and requests for the one-year pilot.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exit safety and Canal Street update
tickets.location_raw: Manhattan Bridge exits; foot of Manhattan Bridge
tickets.summary: A letter was sent to the mayor and DOT about safety concerns at the foot of the Manhattan Bridge, citing a recent crash and death of a community member there. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign, which has not had an update since January. Action: Await responses from the mayor and DOT and press for the Canal Street redesign update and bridge exit safety measures.
